request: Make search fast. Customers give up when they search the menu. It belongs under Feature #50 (Menu).

exchanges.say: You want search to feel fast. Today /menu/search filters every product in lib/search.ts on each keystroke, and no API budget or search test exists (gap:api-budget, gap:tests:/menu). "Fast" needs an action, a number, and conditions; three questions.

questions.ask: Which action must be fast: the first load of /menu/search, typing in the box, or opening a result?
questions.default: Typing until the matching products show, measured from the keystroke, because that is what people feel.

questions.ask: What number must it meet, and for whom: typical users (p50) or nearly everyone (p95)? There is no API budget configured today.
questions.default: p95, with a number from you.

questions.ask: Under what conditions: the seeded menu, a mid-range laptop, a local network?
questions.default: The seeded menu on a mid-range laptop on a local network, because proof captures run on seeded data only.

answers.text: Typing in the menu search box until the matching products show. That's what customers complain about.
Results should show within 200 ms of a keystroke for most people, say p95.

exchanges.say: Got it: typing to results, p95 within 200 ms, on the seeded menu. Three on proof and scope, and one idea.

questions.ask: How do we prove it: a benchmark test on the seeded menu, or the search_performed event in analytics?
questions.default: A repeatable benchmark on the seeded data, recorded as a metric.

questions.ask: While results load, what should people see? Today there is no loading state on /menu/search.
Should a CI budget stop search from getting slow again?
questions.default: Not in this story; park it.

questions.ask: lib/search.ts scans every product on every keystroke. Cache results per query as part of this?

answers.text: A benchmark test on the seeded menu is fine as proof.
Leave the loading feedback as it is.
Not sure we need a CI budget yet; leave it open.
That is not part of what I asked for; park it.

exchanges.say: Here is what done looks like: on the seeded menu of 40 products, typing in /menu/search shows the matching products within 200 ms of each keystroke at p95, proven by a benchmark test. It assumes a mid-range laptop on a local network. A CI budget is deferred; caching and new loading feedback are parked.
